title: Jesus’ rebuke of Peter. Part 4
scripture_text: ‘’From that time on Jesus began to explain to his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things at the hands of the elders, the chief priests and the teachers of the law, and that he must be killed and on the third day be raised to life. Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him. “Never, Lord!” he said. “This shall never happen to you!”
devotional:
Jesus turned and said to Peter, “Get behind me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to me; you do not have in mind the concerns of God, but merely human concerns.” Then Jesus said to his disciples, “Whoever wants to be my disciple, must deny themselves and take up their cross and follow me. For whoever wants to save their life will lose it, but whoever loses their life for me will find it. What good will it be for someone to gain the whole world, yet forfeit their soul? Or what can anyone give in exchange for their soul? For the Son of Man is going to come in his Father’s glory with his angels, and then he will reward each person according to what they have done.’’

So how do we become cross bearers?

a. We must deny ourselves.

What does it men to deny yourself?

Many people think that to deny yourself means that we must feel bad about ourselves, we must loathe ourselves, we must suffer from a poor self image. However, those who think this way are unable to deny themselves. Denying yourself is an expression of security not insecurity, it is a volitional choice of our wills, not an emotional response to the world around us. When we fall into the trap of equating a low self-image with self-denial we are doing the complete opposite to what we think we are doing. People who suffer from chronic self-image problems can become self-obsessed and very selfish, which in turn prevents self-denial.

The Greek word for deny is arneomai means, disown, renounce, refuse, not to accept, to reject, to refuse something offered, it carries the idea of making a volitional choice. It is best illustrated in the words of Philippians 2:6-8 'Who being in very nature God, did not consider equality with God something to be grasped. But made himself nothing, taking the very nature of a servant, being made in human likeness. And being found in the appearance of a man he humbled himself, and became obedient to death even death on a cross.'

To deny yourself is to choose being a servant over having position of authority. To deny yourself is to choose humility over pride. To deny yourself is to choose to obey the will of God irrespective of the personal cost and pain.

What kind of person would find it really difficult to choose to take up their cross? the person who is insecure because of a bad self image, the person who hasn't accepted themselves, so they desperately try to find life in other things and in other people rather than in God. To deny yourself is an expression of self acceptance and contentment.

What are the consequences of denying your self?

You will be able to take up your cross because your focus will not be on your self; you will have a spontaneous, automatic disposition to live a life of self-sacrifice so you can serve others.

You will discover real life. Jesus says four things about life, (Greek psyche) in these verses.

Whoever desires to save his life [psyche] will lose it.

Whoever loses his life [psyche] for Christ's sake will find it.

What profit is it to a man if he gains the whole world, and loses his own life [psyche?]

What will a man give in exchange for his life [psyche?]

Jesus is not saying that taking up our cross will save us from an eternity without him. That would suggest that we can earn our salvation. By commanding us to take up our crosses, He is wanting us to live with the same heart attitude that He had on the cross.

b. You will loose your life

So what does it mean to loose your life and save your life?

All believers have eternal life. However, only ‘self-denying’ believers will realise the full potential of eternal life (John 10:10). A 'saved life' is the glory of a life lived for God.

To loose one's life is to play it safe; it is to decide against the way of the cross and its conform with the status quo. It is to decide to play it safe, it is a deep concern for self-interest. "Survival at all costs," is a flawed philosophy by which to live. 'Be faithful to Christ no matter what the cost,' is the philosophy Jesus' disciples need to live by. We are made in such away, that when we live a self-obsessed life, something within us dies. We have been made to live lives for the benefit of others, and that is only possible when we live a cross shaped life. "Jesus is not anti-our-life; he is anti-preoccupation-with-our-life" (Bruner, 593

'There are two attitudes toward life which are possible, and you can have only one or the other.'

One is to save your life now, i.e., hoard it, clutch it, cling to it, grasp it, try to get hold of it for yourself, take care of yourself, trust yourself, see that in every situation your first and major concern is, 'What's in it for me’ The other attitude is: lose it, i.e., fling it away, disregard what advantages there may be for you in a situation, and move out in dependence upon God, careless of what may happen to you.' Ray Steadman. cdn.pbc.org. Accessed 31/07/25
prayer: Father help me to loose my life.
